title: Crewship panel payload — table.v1
description: Declared columns and keyed rows, rendered as a semantic table that collapses to a card list in a narrow container. Pushed by a routine or by a script running inside a crew container. Cells hold scalars only — there is no cell type that carries markup, a URL or a nested structure, because a table is the panel most likely to be filled from data the producer did not write. The server attaches the timestamp, the run id and the producer identity; freshness is computed from the timestamp the server stored.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (informational; the server ignores it). Present so a hand-written payload gets inline validation in an editor while a producer script is being developed.

columns.description: The columns, in render order. Declared once per push and not inferred from the rows, so a push that happens to return no rows still renders a table with headings rather than an empty box.

rows.description: The rows, in the order they should be rendered — the producer sorts, because the panel has no query with which to sort anything. Required even when empty: an empty array is a measured "nothing matched", while an absent one is a producer that stopped halfway. Bounded at 500, above which the answer is a narrower query in the producer, not a longer table on the page.

key.description: The key this column's cells are stored under in every row. Lowercase alpha-num plus hyphen/underscore, 1-64 chars — the same slug shape the rest of Crewship uses. Unique within the payload: two columns sharing a key means one of them can never be filled.

label.description: The heading a human reads. Written in the workspace's language by the producing agent; nothing is translated at render time.

align.description: Cell alignment. Numbers belong on the right so their digits line up; omit it and text alignment is used.

Row.description: One row, keyed by column key. This is the one object in the panel vocabulary whose property NAMES are data rather than schema, so it cannot use `additionalProperties: false` — instead the key shape is constrained here and the server checks, after this schema passes, that every key names a declared column and that every declared column is present. A key with no column would be delivered to the client and rendered nowhere; an absent column would be indistinguishable from a measured null.

additionalProperties.description: One cell. Scalars only: no markup, no URL, no image, no nested object — a table cell is where untrusted data most often lands, and none of those can be rendered safely from a payload an agent may have been talked into writing. `null` is no data and renders as an em dash, which is a different claim from `0` or an empty string.
